subject: Forrester briefing request / customer case-call with Acme Cloud
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@forrester.com>
To: sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Brief 30-min customer conversation request

Hi Sofia,

I hope you are well. I’m putting together a short vendor profile for a Forrester briefing focused on production-scale LLM inference, and I’d like to include a validated customer perspective. Would one of your customers be available for a 30-minute phone call between May 17-21 to discuss:

- Why they chose Redwood for inference
- Typical workloads and SLA/latency considerations
- Cost/efficiency and operational lessons learned
- Any integration or security considerations for regulated data

If possible, please send a candidate contact (name, role, best email/phone) and any standard reference guidelines you ask customers to follow. No proprietary code or raw logs are requested; we’re looking for a candid product and operational perspective.

Thanks — happy to work around calendars.

Best,
Lena Park
Senior Analyst, AI Platforms
Forrester Research
lena.park@forrester.com

--
Note: Forrester occasionally records these calls for note-taking; we can accommodate a brief non-attribution request if your customer prefers.

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Mike Jansen <mike.jansen@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, Lena Park <lena.park@forrester.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brief 30-min customer conversation request (Forrester)

Hi Mike,

Quick favor to ask: Forrester is requesting a short (30-min) conversation with one of our production customers to better understand LLM-serving experiences. I asked them for times the week of May 17-21.

Would you or a member of your platform/ML infra team be willing to speak? Topics they’re interested in are listed below. We have a short guideline document (attached) that describes the scope and how attribution/capture is handled.

Proposed scope:
- Why Acme chose Redwood and the key evaluation criteria
- Typical latency / throughput profiles and how you manage cost
- Any integration or security items (KMS, VPC, audit logs)
- Top three operational lessons for engineering teams

Practical notes:
- Call is usually ~30 minutes, analyst-led; Forrester may take notes or record with permission
- Redwood will coordinate scheduling and will share the final attendee list and questions ahead of time
- We can support legal review of the question set; see attached draft Qs

If you’re open, could you propose 2-3 30-min windows next week? If you prefer, someone else on your team is fine to join.

Thanks so much for considering — we really appreciate customers being generous with reference time.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Customer Programs
Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
Attachment: acme-reference-guidelines.pdf
